name: Vegetable Pulao
description: Vegetable Pulao is an aromatic rice dish cooked with mixed vegetables, whole spices, and herbs. It can be served for lunch or dinner with raita.
ingredients: Whole spices and coriander leaves as desired
instructions: Wash the basmati rice thoroughly and soak it for 15 minutes. Drain before cooking.
Heat oil or ghee in a pot and add cumin seeds and whole spices.
Add sliced onion and cook until it becomes lightly golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook briefly.
Add carrots, beans, and green peas. Saute for 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the drained rice and mix gently.
Add water and salt. Adjust the water according to the rice variety.
Cover and cook on low heat until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed.
Let the pulao rest for 5 minutes, fluff gently, and garnish with coriander.
health_benefits: Rice provides carbohydrates for energy.
Carrots and peas provide fibre and various micronutrients.
Mixed vegetables contribute to dietary variety.
substitutions: Use other vegetables such as cauliflower or sweet corn.
Use oil instead of ghee for a dairy-free version.

name: Masala Dosa
description: Masala Dosa is a thin, crispy dosa made from fermented rice and urad dal batter and filled with a spiced potato mixture.
instructions: Boil the potatoes until tender, peel them, and mash them roughly.
Heat oil in a pan and add mustard seeds and curry leaves.
Add sliced onion and green chilli. Saute until the onion softens.
Add turmeric, salt, and mashed potatoes. Mix well and cook for a few minutes.
Heat a flat dosa pan and lightly grease it.
Pour a ladle of dosa batter onto the pan and spread it into a thin circle.
Cook until the underside becomes golden and crisp.
Place some potato filling in the centre and fold the dosa.
Serve hot with chutney and sambar.
health_benefits: Rice and potatoes provide carbohydrates.
Urad dal contributes plant protein.
Fermented batter is used in traditional dosa preparation.
substitutions: Use less oil when cooking the dosa.
Adjust chilli according to your preferred spice level.

name: Idli
description: Idli is a soft, steamed South Indian dish made using fermented rice and urad dal batter. It is commonly served with sambar and chutney.
ingredients: A little oil for greasing the moulds
instructions: Prepare fermented idli batter or use ready-made batter.
Lightly grease the idli moulds.
Pour batter into each mould without filling it completely.
Add water to the steamer and bring it to a boil.
Place the idli stand inside the steamer.
Steam for approximately 10 to 15 minutes, depending on the mould size.
Check that the idlis are cooked through.
Allow them to cool slightly before removing them from the moulds.
Serve warm with sambar and chutney.
health_benefits: Steaming requires little added oil.
Rice provides carbohydrates.
Urad dal contributes protein.
substitutions: Serve with vegetable sambar for additional vegetables.
Use a suitable alternative batter if a dietary restriction requires it.

name: Paneer Butter Masala
description: Paneer Butter Masala is a creamy tomato-based curry prepared with paneer, butter, cream, and aromatic Indian spices.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute the chopped onion until soft.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook briefly.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, chilli powder, and salt.
Cook until the tomatoes become soft and form a thick mixture.
Allow the mixture to cool slightly, then blend until smooth.
Return the sauce to the pan.
Add butter, garam masala, and a little water if needed.
Add paneer cubes and simmer gently for 3 to 5 minutes.
Stir in cream and warm through without boiling vigorously.
Garnish with coriander and serve with roti, naan, or rice.
health_benefits: Paneer provides protein and calcium.
Tomatoes contribute vitamin C and other micronutrients.
The nutritional profile depends on the quantities of butter and cream used.
substitutions: Use less butter and cream to reduce the amount of added fat.
Use a suitable plant-based alternative if avoiding dairy.

name: Aloo Gobi
description: Aloo Gobi is a traditional Indian dish made with potatoes, cauliflower, onions, tomatoes, and aromatic spices.
instructions: Wash the vegetables thoroughly.
Peel and cube the potatoes and separate the cauliflower into florets.
Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds.
Add onion and saute until softened.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook briefly.
Add tomato, turmeric, coriander powder, and salt.
Cook until the tomato softens.
Add potatoes and cauliflower and mix gently.
Add a small amount of water and cover the pan.
Cook on low to medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are tender.
Garnish with coriander and serve with roti or rice.
health_benefits: Cauliflower provides fibre and vitamin C.
Potatoes provide carbohydrates and potassium.
Using a variety of vegetables contributes to a varied diet.

name: Vegetable Upma
description: Vegetable Upma is a savoury South Indian dish made with roasted semolina, vegetables, mustard seeds, curry leaves, and mild spices.
instructions: Dry-roast the semolina over low heat until lightly aromatic, then set aside.
Heat oil or ghee in a pan.
Add mustard seeds and allow them to crackle.
Add curry leaves, chopped onion, and green chilli.
Add the mixed vegetables and cook until they begin to soften.
Pour in water and add salt.
Bring the water to a boil.
Slowly add the roasted semolina while stirring continuously to prevent lumps.
Reduce the heat and cover the pan.
Cook until the water is absorbed and the semolina becomes soft.
Garnish with coriander and serve warm.
health_benefits: Semolina provides carbohydrates.
Mixed vegetables contribute fibre and micronutrients.
The amount of added oil affects the total fat content.
substitutions: Use a suitable gluten-free grain instead of semolina if needed.
Add more vegetables according to preference.

name: Kadai Paneer
description: Kadai Paneer is a North Indian curry made with paneer, capsicum, tomatoes, onions, and freshly ground coriander and cumin spices.
instructions: Dry-roast coriander seeds and cumin seeds until fragrant.
Crush the roasted spices coarsely and set them aside.
Heat oil in a pan and saute the sliced onion until lightly golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for about one minute.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, chilli powder, salt, and crushed spices.
Cook until the tomatoes soften and form a thick masala.
Add capsicum and a little water.
Cook until the capsicum is slightly tender but still holds its shape.
Add paneer cubes and garam masala.
Mix gently and simmer for 3 to 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve with roti, naan, or rice.
health_benefits: Paneer contributes protein and calcium.
Capsicum and tomatoes provide various micronutrients.
The dish's total fat depends on the paneer and oil quantities.
substitutions: Adjust chilli powder to control the spice level.
Use a suitable plant-based paneer alternative if avoiding dairy.

name: Tomato Curry
description: Tomato Curry is a simple, tangy Indian curry prepared with tomatoes, onions, ginger, garlic, and aromatic spices.
instructions: Wash and chop the tomatoes and onion.
Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds.
Add the onion and saute until softened.
Add garlic and ginger and cook briefly.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, coriander powder, and salt.
Cook until the tomatoes become soft.
Add a little water and simmer until the curry reaches the desired consistency.
Mash or blend the mixture if a smoother texture is preferred.
Garnish with coriander leaves.
Serve with rice, chapati, or dosa.
health_benefits: Tomatoes provide vitamin C and lycopene.
Onions contribute flavour and small amounts of micronutrients.
The dish can be served with other foods to make a balanced meal.
substitutions: Reduce chilli or spices to suit your preference.
Add cooked vegetables or legumes for variety.
